messages:
incident-bot: [PAGE] HIGH SEV - Dedicated pool 'thalia-enterprise-pool' GPU util >= 99% for 3m. Tenant: thalia-enterprise (VPC). Queue depth increasing. Paging sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: On it. Paging eng/runtime and CS. @emily-cs please confirm customer impact.

emily-cs: Thalia reporting latency spikes and intermittent 503s on inference endpoints. They say it's affecting product search. CS on call with them now.

raj: Looking at infra: pool GPUs at 99-100% across nodes. ~22 active inference pods. One pod stuck Pending earlier but main issue is sustained request surge from the tenant — token/sec ~4x baseline, steady.

lee: Can we use burst capacity? Current pool config shows burst_enabled=false. If we flip it we can spill to shared warm nodes but need approval (may increase cross-tenant risk).

ops-manager: Proposal: short emergency burst + scale up dedicated by +2 GPUs if quota allows, and throttle non-SLA routes. Need confirmation of SLO from CS.

emily-cs: Thalia is premium enterprise, SLO 99.9 latency. They want minimal disruption.

sre-oncall: Decision (temporary): enable emergency burst for 20 minutes to clear queue, submit autoscale request for +2 GPUs, and apply a temporary rate-limit to low-priority routes (batch-*). Raj/Lee please implement. I'll notify customer and track.

raj: Checking nodes and GPU stats now.

# quick checks
kubectl get pods -n pools-thalia
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu --format=csv -l
# result: 99,99,100,99 across g0-g3

raj: Executing changes now:
```
# enable burst via control plane
curl -X POST 'https://control-plane.internal/api/pools/thalia/burst' -d '{"enable":true,"duration":1200}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>'
# submit autoscale request
curl -X POST 'https://infra.internal/autoscale-requests' -d '{"pool":"thalia","add_gpus":2}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

lee: Autoscale request accepted; cloud quota in us-west-2 shows availability for +2 GPUs. Spinning up nodes now. ETA ~3m for nodes + kube join.

sre-oncall: Applying route limit for low-priority traffic: `redwoodctl routes set thalia batch-* --qps 4 --reason 'incident mitigation'`

emily-cs: Notified Thalia support: "We are enabling emergency burst and adding capacity; expect a short window of degraded throughput while we throttle noncritical routes. We'll send an update in 15m."

thalia-sre: Thanks — we'll pause scheduled backfills and noncritical retries on our side.

ops-manager: Monitoring: queue length trending down from 430 -> 80 within 4m after burst + throttle. GPU util dropping to ~78% as nodes come up.

sre-oncall: Good progress. Keep an eye for any new heavy consumers. Create incident postmortem ticket and assign to raj + lee. If queue doesn't stabilize in 15m we'll extend burst or mix in preemptible instances.

emily-cs: CS will send a customer note to Thalia's PAM and schedule a follow-up 1:1 to review root cause and smoothing options.

incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Duration so far: 12m. Page will be auto-closed if no regressions in 30m.

sre-oncall: Handoff: I'm handing watch to lee for 30m. I'm available if escalation needed, but leaving the channel. @lee please ack and monitor.

lee: Ack. Will watch metrics and escalate to oncall-2 if spike resumes. Adding runbook note in /incidents/11623 with the commands used.

thalia-sre: Appreciate the fast response. We'll report any residual errors here.

sre-oncall: Closing loop for now — postmortem assigned, customer notified, mitigation in place.
